product_from_film: ramAIn moves data between business applications by operating their interfaces, illustrated with invoice processing.
explains_well: An approved invoice is opened, structured, entered into an ERP form and sent, with the same invoice number recurring.
unclear: The film shows the agent learning interface fields but not how a user defines and starts this workflow.
scenario: Find an approved partner invoice, extract its data, populate an internal invoice form and send it.
product_clear_basis: Visible text says it uses a computer like a human to move data across portals, legacy systems and desktop apps by 22s.

categories.finding: Stage labels, structured table and sent confirmation communicate the main workflow without verified sound.
Green outlines and an agent-labeled cursor point to the active field, while status pills explain the larger operation.
The invoice example receives about 48s, with enough states to show header and line-item entry. The first 31s delay that concrete task.
The API-limit premise is answered by a visible cross-application form flow ending in sent confirmation. The actual no-API mechanism is not proven.
Scattered words and failure framing give way to orderly fields and a check toast, suggesting resolution; response is unmeasured.
The recurring invoice number and line-item table link source and target better than the later generic integrations diagram.
The film shows data-entry and sent states. Actual delivery, field accuracy, no-API operation, comparative speed and universal compatibility are unverified.
Field recognition and an end-to-end invoice example make the automation category concrete; the bowl mark adds identity.
Show how this workflow starts.
